body.en:
Question B-001-023-003.

Why the correct answer is right: If an ISED-defined exclusion criterion applies, the operator may not be required to contact the land-use authority to determine public consultation requirements. The key is that the exclusion comes from the applicable procedure, not from convenience.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "In a rural area": Rural location alone is not the exclusion criterion identified by the official answer.
- sourceIndex 2: "When the structure is part of an amateur radio antenna": Amateur use does not by itself remove antenna-siting consultation responsibilities.
- sourceIndex 3: "When transmitting will only be done at low power": Low transmitter power is not the antenna-consultation exclusion named in this item.
